1. Core Clinical Tension: A 79-year-old rural female farmer presents with 3 months of upper abdominal discomfort, weakness, weight loss, hypoproteinemia, gastric mucosal thickening, retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and polyserosal effusions (pericardial, bilateral pleural, pelvic, and ascites). While endoscopic findings and subsequent biopsy demonstrate gastric MALT lymphoma, this indolent lymphoma cannot account for widespread polyserosal effusions or profound systemic deterioration, creating an urgent search for a coexistent aggressive malignancy or chronic disseminated infection.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission workup ends with baseline blood tests showing hypoproteinemia, negative urea breath test, ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT showing the gastric mass, retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and polyserosal effusions, and endoscopic visualization of gastric mucosal erosion and cobblestone changes, immediately prior to mucosal biopsy histopathology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Gastric adenocarcinoma or aggressive intravascular large B-cell lymphoma was initially considered due to widespread serosal effusions and gastric lesion; however, review of serial biopsies demonstrated classic epithelioid granulomas, caseous necrosis, and acid-fast bacilli, establishing coexisting peritoneal and gastric tuberculosis.
case_prompt:
A 79-year-old female rural agricultural worker presented with a 3-month history of progressive upper abdominal discomfort, unintentional weight loss, and generalized weakness. Her past medical history was notable for hypertension, nephrolithiasis, and chronic gastritis treated with antihypertensives and proton pump inhibitors. She denied any history of diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, viral hepatitis, chronic viral infections, familial malignancies, prior surgeries, tobacco smoking, or alcohol use. She reported no fever, night sweats, or superficial lymphadenopathy.

Physical examination revealed an elderly woman with signs of temporal wasting but no palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, or peripheral edema. Heart sounds were regular without murmurs or friction rubs, and chest auscultation revealed diminished breath sounds at the lung bases.

Laboratory evaluation revealed significant hypoproteinemia. A carbon-14 urea breath test was negative. Bedside ultrasonography and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed marked wall thickening of the gastric body concerning for gastric malignancy, extensive retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and marked polyserosal effusions comprising pericardial effusion, bilateral pleural effusions, pelvic effusion, and moderate ascites.

Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed mucosal erosion, wall thickening, and superficial cobblestone-like lesions along the anterior wall of the gastric body.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Aggressive Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma / Gastric Carcinoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Widespread polyserosal effusions and gastric wall thickening in an elderly patient suggested an aggressive metastatic malignancy or intravascular lymphoma; however, biopsy showed an indolent MALT lymphoma with reactive intravascular plasmablasts lacking light-chain restriction, which still could not explain the polyserosal effusions.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: However, MALT lymphoma, as an indolent lymphoma, seemed to be incompatible with the patient's systemic symptoms. Aggressive intravascular lymphoma cannot still be completely excluded.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although gastric biopsy and PCR confirmed monoclonal immunoglobulin gene rearrangements diagnostic of MALT lymphoma, indolent low-grade lymphoma fails to cause acute multisystem polyserositis with pericardial, pleural, and ascitic effusions.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: However, MALT lymphoma, as an indolent lymphoma, seemed to be incompatible with the patient's systemic symptoms.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic breakthrough occurred on retrospective pathological review of serial gastric biopsy specimens, which demonstrated conspicuous caseous necrosis, multinucleated Langhans giant cells, and acid-fast bacilli, confirming concurrent disseminated gastrointestinal and serosal tuberculosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Unexpectedly, conspicuous caseous necrosis, epithelioid granulomas (shown in Fig. 4a), multinucleated giant cells (shown in Fig. 4b), and two acid-fast Bacilli were found in her previous biopsy, highly suggestive of tuberculosis, but the initial diagnosis referred to chronic granulomatous inflammation.

editor_comments: Admission clinical presentation cleanly ends at endoscopic visualization and admission staging CT/ultrasound. Biopsy details, immunohistochemistry, and AFB findings are contained in diagnostic reasoning.
